School vocabulary
Sort out
Separate things into groups — Clasificar / ordenar.
She sorted out the papers by date.
School vocabulary
Set up
Trick someone into appearing guilty — Tender una trampa a / incriminar.
He says the police set him up.
School vocabulary
Stick out
Be very noticeable — Destacar / llamar la atención.
Her accent sticks out here.
School vocabulary
Wake up
Realise the truth about something — Darse cuenta / abrir los ojos.
He finally woke up to the danger.
School vocabulary
Get up
Stand up from sitting or lying — Ponerse de pie / levantarse.
Everyone got up when she entered.
Move up to a higher place — Subir.
We got up to the top of the hill by noon.
School vocabulary
Sit down
Make someone sit, usually for a serious talk — Sentar a alguien.
His parents sat him down and explained.
School vocabulary
Go out
Stop burning or shining — Apagarse.
The fire went out during the night.
Go somewhere together romantically — Salir juntos.
They have been going out for a year.
School vocabulary
Come back
Become successful again after difficulty — Resurgir / remontar.
The team came back in the second half.
Become popular again — Volver a ponerse de moda.
Wide trousers are coming back.
School vocabulary
Go back
Date from a certain time — Remontarse a.
This custom goes back to the Middle Ages.
School vocabulary
Pick up
Lift something with your hand — Levantar / coger.
Pick up that book, please.
Learn a skill or habit easily — Aprender sin esfuerzo / coger.
She picked up Italian in six months.
School vocabulary
Drop off
Fall in amount or interest — Disminuir / caer.
Sales dropped off after Christmas.
School vocabulary
Turn on
Attack someone you were friendly with — Volverse contra.
The dog turned on its owner.
Make someone interested or excited — Atraer / entusiasmar.
Jazz has never turned me on.
School vocabulary
Turn off
Leave a road you are travelling on — Desviarse de / salir de.
Turn off at the next junction.
Make someone lose interest — Quitar las ganas a / echar para atrás.
The price turned me off completely.
School vocabulary
Put away
Send someone to prison — Encerrar / meter en la cárcel.
They put him away for five years.
Eat or drink a large amount — Zamparse / meterse entre pecho y espalda.
He can put away three pizzas.
School vocabulary
Wash up
Be carried to the shore by water — Llegar a la orilla / varar.
A whale washed up on the beach.
School vocabulary
Check out
Pay and leave a hotel — Dejar el hotel / hacer el check-out.
We check out at eleven.
Pay for your shopping at the till — Pasar por caja.
She checked out with twelve items.
School vocabulary
Come in
Arrive, of a train or plane — Llegar.
The flight came in an hour late.
Be useful — Venir bien / resultar útil.
A spare key always comes in handy.
School vocabulary
Go away
Disappear or get much less — Desaparecer / írsele a uno.
The pain went away after an hour.
Leave home for a while — Irse / marcharse unos días.
They went away for the weekend.
School vocabulary
Hang up
Hang something so it does not touch the ground — Colgar.
Hang up your coat in the hall.
School vocabulary
Pick out
Recognise something among others — Distinguir / identificar.
I picked out his voice in the crowd.
